# Choose the scientific preference

The experimental continuous policies guide semantic item selection using a
declared structural proxy. They retain the supplied factor count and intended
item assignments. They do not discover dimensionality, repair the meaning of
embeddings, or predict participant-response validity by themselves.

| ESEM score mode | Utility | Preference |
|---|---|---|
| `continuous_structure` | Structure | Intended loading strength and separation from cross-loadings |
| `continuous_reconstruction` | Reconstruction | Approximation of the selected input matrix |
| `continuous_balanced` | Harmonic mean of structure and reconstruction | Both organization and approximation |

The existing `current` and `structure_weighted` modes retain their definitions.
No continuous policy is declared universally best. Reconstruction does not
directly reward the intended grouping; structure rewards it explicitly.

# Exact definitions

For item i, let p be its absolute standardized loading on the intended aligned
factor, and c its largest absolute cross-loading. Average each item measurement
within each intended factor, then average the factor means equally. A factor
does not receive extra weight simply because it has more selected items.

```text
strength   = equal_factor_mean(min(1, p))
separation = equal_factor_mean(min(1, max(0, p - c)))
structure  = harmonic_mean(strength, separation)
```

For one factor, separation is inapplicable and structure equals strength.
The unit cap bounds a decision utility; it is not an acceptance cutoff or a
claim that every admissible oblique loading must lie below one.

Compare the correlation matrix supplied to ESEM with the fitted model's implied
correlation matrix. Use each off-diagonal pair once:

```text
raw_reconstruction = 1 - sum((observed - implied)^2) / sum(observed^2)
reconstruction     = max(0, min(1, raw_reconstruction))
```

Identity is the explicit zero-association baseline. The raw improvement and both
sums of squares are retained. If all observed off-diagonals are zero, the raw
ratio is undefined (`NA`) and utility is zero because there is no association
signal to improve over that baseline. Required unavailable measurements produce
an unavailable objective; they receive no neutral reward. Negative loading
margins and reconstruction worse than baseline have a zero utility floor, so
weak candidates can tie. The harmonic mean is zero when a component is zero.

These formulas use no conventional loading bands, fit-index, AVE, or HTMT
cutoffs. They still express explicit optimization preferences. Factor
correlations remain estimates and affect fitted geometry indirectly.

# Configure scoring and guard roles separately

```{r eval=FALSE}
esem_options <- semantica_esem_config(score_mode = "continuous_balanced")
quality_options <- semantica_quality_config(
  psychometric_guard_action = "report_only",
  final_selection_mode = "scalar"
)
diagnostic_options <- semantica_diagnostics_config(final_fit = "off")

# Supply these as esem, quality, and diagnostics to semantica_run_custom().
# Existing text/vector workflows can instead use ACO_with_ESEM() directly:
# semantic_esem_score_mode = "continuous_balanced"
# psychometric_guard_action = "report_only"
```

When quality options are omitted, continuous modes resolve to report-only guards
and scalar final selection. Explicit quality settings take precedence. A
separately declared hard guard remains available for a sensitivity condition.

Report-only keeps reference values, exceedances, and unavailable states visible.
Its guard multiplier is one; guard rejection, structural repair, and the legacy
diagnostic bonus are inactive. `reference_guard_passed` or
`structural_guard$passed` is descriptive. Participant-validation eligibility is
`NA`, with status `not_assessed_report_only`. A legacy ESEM score still includes
its reference-based terms when paired with report-only guards.

The separate semantic objective, content/facet constraints, mathematical
admissibility, and any separately configured PFA objective remain active.
Continuous scoring changes the ESEM component of the mixture. For example,
`esem_weight = 0.5` still combines it with the other search component. Existing
checkpoint reliability adjustment can lower effective ESEM weight when fits
fail; inspect recorded effective weights and fallback states.

Search DFI is skipped because these utilities do not use its cutoffs. Explicitly
requested post-selection DFI/DDDFI remains separately configurable and can be
expensive. The fitter still uses a declared reference N; these utilities add no
respondent interpretation or guarantee of numerical invariance.

# Reuse recorded inputs and control cost

`semantica_prepare_inputs()` freezes recorded item and definition vectors for
provider-free native replay. See the [existing-item workflow](semantica-user-workflows.html)
for the full recipe. Preparation discards supplied evaluation/pass columns and
recomputes native alignment and representation diagnostics. Blueprint,
representation, source-definition, and mutation checks protect replay identity;
the pool cannot silently expand through generation top-up.

Use `semantica_resource_config(cpu_cores = 1L)` for a serial worker configuration,
and set explicit ants, total iterations, and search-fit limits. A search-fit
limit counts unique search candidate jobs; archive refits and final diagnostics
have separate counts. One worker is not a guarantee that every numerical
library uses only one system thread.

Continuous archive fits receive candidate-specific seeds derived from the run
seed and item IDs, independent of item order and native character encoding.
Solver tolerances can still permit small numerical differences. Utility schemas
and calibration records distinguish modes; prepare newly versioned runs when
changing policies rather than resuming old scores under a new definition.

# Interpret comparisons on a common basis

Hold the pool, representation, blueprint, counts, constraints, and budgets fixed.
Use several matched optimizer seeds and a constrained random or semantic-only
reference. Report common loading/margin, reconstruction, semantic, coverage,
redundancy, failure, selection-stability, and cost outcomes. Do not rank policies
by their differently defined objective scores or treat those scores as universal
quality certificates. Search-time and archive/final fit counts should both be
included in cost reporting.

An exact two-factor synthetic matrix can reconstruct almost perfectly under
several different item selections. Its reconstruction utility cannot then
distinguish the intended loading organization. With reconstruction fixed at one,
the balanced ESEM utility becomes `2 * structure / (1 + structure)`. This is a
rescaling, not evidence of improved selected items; in a mixture it can also
change tradeoffs against the separate semantic objective.

For direct optimizer results, inspect:

```{r eval=FALSE}
selected$esem_result$continuous_utility
selected$objective_context
selected$structural_guard
selected$evaluation_telemetry
selected$performance
```

For `semantica_run_custom()` results, the optimizer is retained under
`result$advanced$optimization`. Reference attainment, numerical admissibility,
and optional participant-response evidence answer separate questions.

# Other recent controls

- `semantica_generation_config(prompt_history = "omit")` excludes previous
  generated sentence text from prompts while retaining local history checks.
  `history_dedup = "lexical"` also uses the existing character-bigram Jaccard
  threshold of .92; it is lexical duplicate screening, not semantic equivalence.
- `retain_responses = TRUE` retains per-attempt prompts/responses for offline
  audit. This can retain sensitive item text. The default is false. Parser
  accounting separates exact duplicates, lexical duplicates, truncation, and
  retained items.
- `candidate_validator = function(items, context) ...` returns one character
  reason per candidate: `NA` or empty accepts, a nonempty reason rejects.
  Rejections consume the existing bounded retry budget. Invalid returns/errors
  stop generation. Freeze any external resources separately; the callback is
  neither independent validation nor a fully captured external environment.
- `semantica_esem_config(bounds = "pos.var")` explicitly requests nonnegative
  variance estimation with boundary flags and an unconstrained final comparison.
  Use native ESEM/heuristic calibration and `final_fit = "off"`; unsupported
  strict-CFA/DDDFI combinations are rejected. Zero-boundary convergence does
  not establish favorable structure. The default remains `bounds = "none"`.
- `exploration_slots = 1L` reserves a seeded random candidate outside the cheap
  top shortlist when possible, within the existing search-fit budget. Its
  default is zero. Calibration `bootstrap_candidates` controls the bounded
  warm-up candidate limit.
- `semantica_leave_one_scale_out_calibration(..., splits = ...)` accepts frozen
  training memberships for each held-out instrument. Explicit detected item,
  paraphrase, or respondent overlap is rejected. Missing declarations leave
  independence unestablished; pooled and macro-scale summaries remain distinct.
